steps.content: And at last, stillness returns.

The imaging system, it appears, can pick up your movements and Mania signature, feeding the recorded data back through another simulation pass. You've barely exerted yourself, perhaps because the system has nudged things in your favor. Either way, it's over now.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I still don't fully understand what just happened, but... the sensation felt close to Mania. The shackles seemed to recognize it better than I did. They locked right onto those mutation points.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I was mostly just following my gut. I can't really make sense of what I'm feeling on my own. That said, your scientists might be able to. Want to give it a try?
Your earnest invitation doesn't cheer Lemma up. She looks, if anything, even more crestfallen.
Her plummeting mood, however, merely draws an amused smile from the Director.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: It seems there were a few hidden cracks in your theory after all. Not the easiest to spot, I'll admit. So. What will you do now?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Are you really going to waste more time defending yourself? Is it your theory you're trying to protect... or the pride of a <color=#fb9259>genius</color>? ...Chief Scientist.
The genius girl shoots her a scorching glare.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: ...I don't need you to spell it out. I'm heading back.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: The data we just gathered is invaluable. I'll analyze it thoroughly and submit the revised proposal as soon as possible.
The petite blonde girl clicks away in quick little steps. As she passes you by, Isomer's voice, so detestable to her, comes chasing after her from behind.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Where's your gratitude?
Her tone is icy and condescending, with undisguised mockery seeping from every syllable. It seizes the girl mid-step, stopping her dead in her tracks.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Someone here "assisted with your experiment," "identified flaws in your proposal," and "may provide critical support going forward." What sort of attitude should one show toward such a person? Shall I demonstrate? Or perhaps...

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You'd rather stay stuck in this bottleneck? Waste a few more months?

Lemma halts at your side and stands there for what feels like an eternity. Then, rigidly, almost painfully, she twists her head back and speaks—one word at a time, each syllable steeped in humiliation.

steps.speaker: Lemma
steps.content: Thank you... for your assistance... Chief ${PlayerName}... of the Minos Bureau of Crisis Control!
BANG! The door slams shut violently, so much so that it still reverberates as the footsteps skitter away down the hall, chaotic and frantic, like a startled deer in flight.

Before a smile can even form on your lips, Isomer cracks first. She leans against the table, arms folded, shoulders shaking. The dignified Director of the Ring Research Institute has let herself loose, laughing softly before your very eyes.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Hehehe...

steps.speaker: Option
options: So I'm just your teaching aid now? For wrangling difficult children?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Forgive me, that was most unprofessional. Thank you for playing along, Chief. You've given Lemma some genuinely valuable insights to work with.

She dabs at her eyes with a lingering smile, then flicks her hand. A chair glides over, inviting you to sit in it. She takes her own seat across from you, pulls out her terminal, and scrolls through files while playing a few voice messages. It's all the usual: funding, projects, favors sought, and so forth.
Isomer deals with them swiftly, like someone would when sweeping aside trash. She also seems entirely unbothered that you, an outsider, are watching the whole thing.

When the round is done, the smile falls away. The mask reasserts itself, sealing that fleeting moment of openness again. The person sitting across from you right now is, without a doubt, the Director of the Ring Research Institute.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The children's games are over. Now then, let's talk, adult to adult.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You came to see me to push forward your proposal at the EDGE meeting. You want to remove the obstacles standing in the way of suppressing BR-003, don't you?

Just as you thought, she knows everything. The question is, since when? The moment she first approached you in disguise? Or further back still, far enough that she arranged the symposium, anticipating that you would come, far enough that it traces all the way back to some EDGE meeting where the two of you stood toe to toe?
However deep the roots may go, this mission behind enemy lines has finally brought you to the threshold. The time for battle has arrived.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This visit has made everything clear. The Ring Research Institute is fighting to hold onto BR-003 because it's an essential testing site. You have quite a few projects tied directly to it.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And behind every one of those projects is massive research funding, the very thing that's elevated the Institute to where it stands today. You can't afford to let go.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's what EDGE-07 really cares about. They preach science and rationality as the Institute's representative, but it's all a tool in reality. Every argument and every assessment serves one purpose: protecting your interests.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You could've kept this charade going, if I'm being honest. Unfortunately...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Your safety system can't actually protect the Black Ring. It's fundamentally unstable; it can't eliminate every risk. That "anomaly" you just showed me is proof, you know that as well as I do. Ten geniuses won't change anything either. That girl hit a wall a long time ago.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The bottom line is, you have no real grounds to oppose my proposal. BR-003 is far more dangerous than what you've been reporting. It has to be suppressed. I'll personally see to it that all of this is presented to EDGE as evidence in the next meeting.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If you don't want it to come to that, then drop the act. Agree to my proposal. That way—

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Very well. I agree.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: —we'll still have room to negotiate. For example—
[Background + Character Portrait]

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I agree to your proposal. And I'll do everything in my power to support it.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: EDGE values science and rationality. So, before the next vote, I'll prepare all the evidence you'll need to support your position. I'll also deal with the person causing you the greatest obstruction.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Well?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Backing me offers you zero upside—certainly nothing that compensates for losing the Black Ring. I'm not naive enough to believe you'd make a choice like this without weighing what's at stake.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: What makes you so sure?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I've already laid out the logic. And besides...
You meet her eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You don't need to sell me. When it actually counts, at the EDGE meeting, I've seen exactly how 07 votes and what stance they take. That person represents the Institute's interests, and by extension, yours. Isn't that right?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Director</color>?
She offers no direct answer, simply eyeing you as if you were a defiant pupil.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: So that's your reason for infiltrating the Institute after all. You wanted to dig up the identity behind that number. Bold of you. Crossing that particular line takes nerve.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: So, who do you suspect? Want me to give you the answer?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: We've come this far. There's no need to keep dancing around each other.
She looks at you, and slowly, she utters a name.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Heh... I like that answer. Close, but not quite.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Give me a little more time, and I will be EDGE-07. As long as you and I work together to pull down the one sitting in that seat right now.
end

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Lemma Herzfeld</color>.
[Portrait]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's her?!
The shock escapes before you can contain it. Isomer simply watches, savoring your reaction.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Our genius Chief Scientist. Proud, domineering, she always has been. Her arguments are forceful and persuasive. She can always be counted on to provide theoretical cover for every faction's private agenda. And on top of that, she holds considerable sway over the BR-003 Observation Hub...

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: I'm only the Hub's nominal head. A front, something EDGE put in place to obscure 07's true identity. I handle the "trivial tasks" on her behalf. Every decision at the Institute revolves around her. I'm nothing more than a glorified babysitter for the genius.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: That is, of course, when her research is going well. If you want to bring down EDGE-07, you have to strike when she's actually struggling, which is now.

...Struggling? Now that you think of it, that girl indeed seemed anxious. So sensitive, obsessive, and prone to sinking into low spirits—all classic signs of hitting a bottleneck. And the woman before you has taken note of every last one.
[Enter CG]
Isomer has firmly locked onto her prey.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: During the war, the new BR-005 caused disturbances on an unprecedented scale. BR-003 was forced into operation, and its public exposure severely disrupted the stable research environment she relied on. Even now, it remains under frequent attack from unknown sources.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: All I need to do is submit the "incident" we just demonstrated. That would give me grounds to grant you special security clearance as a Mania expert. You'd gain access to the BR-003 Observation Hub and be authorized to participate in the safety inspection.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: And once you're inside, if you want data to prove her theory unreliable, you'll have all the evidence you could ask for. Summer can compile the material and help you build a case to convince EDGE. Doesn't that sound appealing?
Now, the hunter's eyes turn to you.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: From what I gather, of EDGE's eight seats, only the newly appointed 08 openly supports you. And she's already under heavy scrutiny herself. The two of you being seen working too closely together would only invite unnecessary suspicion. For both your sakes, don't play that card lightly.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Beyond her, you have no other allies up there. But I can give you the strongest backing possible. I'll help you defeat EDGE-07 on "rational" grounds. And if it comes to it, I can make sure she disappears from the meeting entirely.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: That will clear every obstacle between you and the Black Ring. BR-003 will be yours to deal with as you see fit.
Her words trail off. She lets the silence settle, waiting for your answer.
You have to give it to her, she knows how to pitch an offer. Everything she lays out is something you need. The moment you remove 07, a clear path forward and success will be within sight.
...And yet, the moment that number finally maps itself onto a real, tangible person, something inside you shifts, leaving you deeply unsettled.

You look back at the Director, and your mind replays the way she teased the girl earlier, the smile that graced her face. Now it all seems as unreal as the persona she wore before. What remains is nothing but cold, ruthless calculus. It is as though a great fissure has yawned open before you, and an icy dread crawls up your spine.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...If we're going to talk cooperation, then I'll need you to be straight with me first.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Was everything with her just a game to you?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Heh. What else would it be?
Jump

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Hehe... I would've thought that by now, after coming all this way to see for yourself, you'd have worked it out.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: At this level, science is power. A genius can transcend both birth and class. This is the last stretch of a golden age, an era when even someone of humble origins can still climb to the top. That's exactly how I worked my way here.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: But then I ran into them. And that was as far as I could go.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Unlike those kids, I'm not one of truth's chosen. I can't compete with a real genius or push the research any further. I can't shape the world the way she does.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: But the moment I stopped fixating on that and looked elsewhere, the view opened right up. Just like now... I've found you, haven't I?
Isomer raises her eyes to you as she speaks. She smiles as she reaches out her hand, her ambition laid utterly bare.

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: The same obstacle stands in our way. Let's remove her together, and we'll both get what we want... And when we do...

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: You get your Black Ring, I get my seat. A perfect win-win. What do you say?

steps.speaker: Isomer
steps.content: Chief ${PlayerName}.

Pixel:

Pixel:
I mean, they've truly mastered the fine arts of stealing other people's work and doctoring data.

Pixel:
These guys are rotten straight through to the roots, and yet they've still got a whole pack of loyal little lapdogs. Hehe, everyone loves riding on someone else's coattails.

Pixel:
Ugh, screw it. I've been swallowing my soul this whole time hyping up United University just to land the gigs. But now that the order's in, this lady is soooo done playing nice.
Science? Truth? Humanity? No, no, no. Our ivory tower doesn't deal in such things.
The true academic sphere runs on money. On power. On who writes whom into the acknowledgments, and whose name is scrubbed from the byline.
It is a brutal, desperate scramble to the top, where you climb or you perish.
